# CLI Evidence: Help

### abx --help

```
$ abx --help
Usage: abx [options] [command]

abx — Agent Sandbox CLI

Create, manage, and interact with cloud sandboxes.

Get started:
  abx config init               Set credentials and region (run first)
  abx create base               Create a sandbox
  abx exec SANDBOX -- CMD...    Run a command in it

Examples:
  abx list --status running
  abx template search python
  abx template scaffold --template python ./my-template
  abx deploy ./my-template

More templates: https://registry.agent-sandbox.cn/templates/

Every action has one canonical path (abx GROUP VERB); the shortcuts below are a
fixed set and cannot be changed in the configuration.

Options:
  --version            Show the version and exit.
  -j, --json           Output as JSON
  -q, --quiet          Minimal output
  -v, --verbose        Verbose output (DEBUG level)
  --no-color           Disable colored output
  --log-level <LEVEL>  Set log level explicitly (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR)
  --ci                 CI/CD mode (quiet + no-color + json)
  -h, --help           Show this message and exit.

Command groups:
  sandbox              Manage sandboxes, their files, processes and commands.
  template             Discover, scaffold, build, publish and install sandbox
                       templates.
  config               Manage persistent credentials and CLI defaults.
  mcp                  Configure and run Agent Sandbox as an MCP server.
  provider             Install, select, configure and run sandbox provider
                       operations.

Sandbox shortcuts:
  create               Create a sandbox. (alias: abx sandbox create)
  list                 List sandboxes. (alias: abx sandbox list)
  info                 Show sandbox details. (alias: abx sandbox info)
  kill                 Terminate sandboxes. (alias: abx sandbox kill)
  exec                 Run a command in a sandbox. (alias: abx sandbox exec)
  connect              Open a terminal in a sandbox. (alias: abx sandbox
                       connect)
  upload               Upload files to a sandbox. (alias: abx sandbox upload)
  download             Download a file from a sandbox. (alias: abx sandbox
                       download)
  run                  Run a registered sandbox command. (alias: abx sandbox
                       command run)
  deploy               Build and publish a template. (alias: abx template
                       deploy)

Provider: alicloud-express (default)
26 provider operations: api-key, quota, sandbox, snapshot, team, volume.
Example: abx provider run api-key.create --help
Use 'abx provider --help' for the directory and 'abx provider run OPERATION --help' for parameters.
Select for one invocation: abx --provider ID provider --help
Exit code: 0
```

### create --help

```
$ abx create --help
Usage: abx create [options] [TEMPLATE_NAME]

Create a new sandbox.

'abx create' is the shortcut of 'abx sandbox create'. A positional argument
selects a template; the default is base. Natural language uses --prompt.

  abx create base                        launch the base template
  abx create code-interpreter-v1         launch an existing template
  abx create --prompt "DESCRIPTION"      generate a template, build and launch

--prompt and an explicit template cannot be combined.

--timeout is the sandbox lifetime in seconds (default: 300).

Examples:
  abx create base              # explicit 'base' template
  abx create python-hello      # named template
  abx create -e API_KEY=xxx -e DEBUG=1    # inject env vars
  abx create --upload ./app --timeout 600 # upload dir, 10-min lifetime
  abx create --prompt "a python data science env"  # generate, build, deploy,
create
  abx create -y --prompt "a node.js api server"    # non-interactive full
pipeline
  abx template scaffold --prompt "a python data science env"  # template files
only

Notes:
  Template generation needs the Qwen Code CLI and a DashScope/ModelStudio
  key ('abx config init --llm'); building and deploying also needs
  'abx config init --build'. It researches publicly verifiable facts
  itself (tool stack, official install method, common dependencies) and
  only asks for private preferences or business decisions it cannot
  infer — one question at a time in interactive sessions. Non-interactive
  shells must pass --yes to generate without asking. Interactive
  sessions are asked up front whether to switch to template init,
  which writes Dockerfile, commands.py, and template.yaml and stops
  before build, push, deploy, and sandbox create. --yes skips that
  question and runs the full pipeline.

Related commands:
  abx list                 List existing sandboxes
  abx info SANDBOX_ID      Inspect a created sandbox
  abx template scaffold DIR    Scaffold a new template project (local)
  abx template scaffold --prompt "DESC" Generate a template only (no build)
  abx template search KEY  Find reusable templates
  abx config init          Set credentials and region

Options:
  --prompt <PROMPT>                Generate a sandbox from a natural-language
                                   description. Mutually exclusive with a
                                   template.
  -T, --template <TEMPLATE>        Template ID or alias to launch (e.g. 'base',
                                   'python-hello'). Defaults to 'base' when
                                   omitted. Cannot be combined with DESCRIPTION.
  -u, --upload <PATH>              Local file or directory to upload after
                                   creation
  -t, --timeout <INTEGER>          Sandbox lifetime in seconds (positive
                                   integer; default: 300)
  --request-timeout <FLOAT>        HTTP request timeout in seconds for the
                                   create call (floor: 120s for cold starts, or
                                   your configured http_timeout if larger).
                                   Increase for very slow sandbox creation.
  -e, --env <ENV>                  Environment variable for the sandbox, format
                                   KEY=VALUE (repeatable)
  -m, --metadata <METADATA>        Metadata key-value pair, format KEY=VALUE
                                   (repeatable)
  --volume-mount <PATH=NAME>       Mount an existing same-Team Volume by name at
                                   an absolute Unix path (Express only;
                                   repeatable)
  -y, --yes                        Skip interactive prompts (the template-only
                                   switch, Qwen Code install, credentials,
                                   description clarification, build/deploy
                                   confirmation) and run the full create
                                   pipeline. Required for template generation in
                                   non-interactive shells.
  --model <MODEL>                  Model id for the template generation step
                                   (for example qwen-coder-plus). Overrides
                                   llm_model / ABX_LLM_MODEL / OPENAI_MODEL for
                                   this command. When the endpoint rejects the
                                   model, an interactive terminal offers coding
                                   and chat models with the arrow keys.
  --acr-namespace <ACR_NAMESPACE>  ACR namespace for building the generated
                                   template (env: ACR_NAMESPACE, or set in .env
                                   file)
  --dir <DIRECTORY>                Parent directory for the generated template
                                   files (Dockerfile, commands.py,
                                   template.yaml); a new <name>-<timestamp>-<id>
                                   subfolder is created inside it. Default:
                                   ~/.abx/generated (an interactive terminal is
                                   asked when omitted).
  -v, --verbose                    Verbose output (DEBUG level)
  -h, --help                       Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### exec --help

```
$ abx exec --help
Usage: abx exec [options] <SANDBOX_ID> <COMMAND...>

Run a command in a sandbox.

'abx exec' is the shortcut of 'abx sandbox exec'.

Put the command after ``--``: it is run exactly as given (no shell).
A single quoted argument is read as a command line, so pipes and
redirects work; use ``sh -c '...'`` for variable expansion.

By default the command runs to completion and abx exits with its remote
exit code. ``--stream`` prints stdout/stderr live while it runs;
``--background`` starts it, prints the pid and returns at once.

Examples:
  abx exec abc123 -- python --version
  abx exec abc123 --cwd /app --timeout 300 -- pytest -q
  abx exec abc123 --env DEBUG=1 -- python app.py
  abx exec abc123 --stream -- pip install numpy
  abx exec abc123 --background -- python -m http.server 8000
  abx exec abc123 "ls /app | wc -l"
  abx --json exec abc123 -- echo ready

Related commands:
  abx connect SANDBOX_ID                  Open the command REPL
  abx sandbox process list SANDBOX_ID     Find a background process
  abx run SANDBOX_ID NAME                 Run a named command registered in the
sandbox

Options:
  --cwd <CWD>              Working directory (empty = container default)
  -e, --env <ENV>          Environment variable for the command, format
                           KEY=VALUE (repeatable)
  -t, --timeout <INTEGER>  Command timeout in seconds (positive integer;
                           default: 60)
  --background             Start the command, print its pid and return without
                           waiting
  --stream                 Print stdout/stderr live while the command runs
  -v, --verbose            Verbose output (DEBUG level)
  -h, --help               Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### run --help

```
$ abx run --help
Usage: abx run [options] <SANDBOX_ID> <COMMAND_NAME>

Run a named command registered in the sandbox.

'abx run' is the shortcut of 'abx sandbox command run'.

Named commands are functions the template registers on the SandboxServer
that runs inside the sandbox (``POST /commands/NAME``). List them with
'abx sandbox command list SANDBOX_ID'. Arguments are validated and
converted by the server according to the registered signature.

Pass arguments with --arg KEY=VALUE (repeatable) and/or --json-args
'{"key": value}' for typed values. The command's return value is printed
(JSON with --json). Fails with a clear error when the sandbox has no
server.

Examples:
  abx run abc123 build
  abx run abc123 test --arg file=tests/
  abx run abc123 add --json-args '{"x": 1, "y": 2}'
  abx --json run abc123 greet --arg name=Ada

Related commands:
  abx sandbox command list SANDBOX_ID   List the registered commands
  abx exec SANDBOX_ID -- CMD            Run an arbitrary command
  abx info SANDBOX_ID                   Inspect the target sandbox

Options:
  -a, --arg <ARGS>         Command argument, format KEY=VALUE (repeatable)
  --json-args <JSON_ARGS>  Command arguments as a JSON object, e.g. '{"x": 1}'
                           (for typed values)
  --server-port <INTEGER>  Port of the SandboxServer inside the sandbox
                           (default: 9000)
  -h, --help               Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### connect --help

```
$ abx connect --help
Usage: abx connect [options] <SANDBOX_ID>

Open an interactive command REPL for a sandbox.

'abx connect' is the shortcut of 'abx sandbox connect'.

This is a line-based REPL, not a PTY: every line you enter runs in a new
process with a 30-second timeout, so ``cd``, environment variables and
aliases do not survive between lines (use ``cd /path && <cmd>`` on one
line, or ``abx exec --cwd``, instead).

On interactive terminals basic line editing and command history are
enabled (Up/Down history, Ctrl+R search, Ctrl+A/E and friends).  Type
``exit``/``quit`` or press Ctrl+D to leave; Ctrl+C also disconnects.
Failed commands are reported as one friendly message - never as raw
HTTP errors.

Examples:
  abx connect abc123

Related commands:
  abx exec SANDBOX_ID -- CMD  Run one command with a custom timeout
  abx info SANDBOX_ID         Inspect connection details

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### provider-update --help

```
$ abx provider update --help
Usage: abx provider update [options] [ID]

Update installed providers from their recorded git source.

Without ID (or with --all) every git-installed provider is checked. A
pinned install stays put unless --ref names a new commit. --check only
reports what would change. Changes to runtime, security, features, config
fields or inherited credentials ask for consent again. A failed handshake
rolls back to the previous version (the data directory is preserved).
Directory and --link installs cannot be updated: reinstall with --force.
The bundled alicloud-express provider follows abx releases. Naming it
reports upgrade guidance, without replacing abx or checking host releases.

Options:
  --ref <REF>                 Git tag, branch or commit to update to
  --check                     Only report available updates
  --all                       Update every installed git provider
  --allow-unpinned            Allow an unpinned update in non-interactive mode
  --allow-insecure-transport  Allow file://, git:// and http:// sources (testing
                              only)
  -y, --yes                   Skip the confirmation prompt
  -h, --help                  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

Options:
  --input <JSON>         JSON input object (default: {})
  --input-file <FILE>    Read JSON input from a file
  -o, --opt <KEY=VALUE>  Provider option (repeatable)
  --region <REGION>      Cloud region for this command
  --yes                  Confirm a write or delete operation
  -h, --help             Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### config-set --help

```
$ abx config set --help
Usage: abx config set [options] <KEY> [VALUE]

Set a configuration value: KEY [VALUE].

Settings are stored in ~/.abx/config.toml, except credentials
(sandbox_api_key, access_key_id, access_key_secret, acr_namespace,
llm_api_key, github_token) which are
written to ~/.abx/.env using their environment-variable names. Setting
llm_api_key also removes any legacy config.toml copy of it (the secret
migrates to the 0600-protected ~/.abx/.env storage).

Passing an empty VALUE clears the stored value for KEY instead: the key
falls back to its built-in default or becomes not set. An empty string
is never stored as a credential or override. Environment variables that
are still exported keep overriding the key at runtime; their values are
never printed. Clearing llm_api_key removes both the ~/.abx/.env entry
and any legacy config.toml copy.

In an interactive terminal VALUE may be omitted: sensitive keys
(github_token, sandbox_api_key, access_key_secret, llm_api_key) are then
read through the masked (asterisk) input and the typed value is never
echoed; other keys use a visible prompt. Pressing Enter at the prompt
cancels without changing anything. In CI / non-interactive sessions
VALUE is required.

Available keys (expected value):
  sandbox_api_key    Sandbox service API key (string; env var
                     ABX_SANDBOX_API_KEY).
                     ``api_key`` is accepted as an alias.
  access_key_id      Alibaba Cloud AccessKey ID for AK/SK auth, used by
                     template deploy and ACR push (string)
  access_key_secret  Alibaba Cloud AccessKey Secret for AK/SK auth, used by
                     template deploy and ACR push (string)
  acr_namespace      ACR namespace for template build, push, and install
                     (string; stored in ~/.abx/.env as ACR_NAMESPACE)
  api_url            Platform API URL (e.g.
https://api.cn-hangzhou.e2b.fc.aliyuncs.com)
  domain             Envd data-plane domain (e.g.
cn-hangzhou.e2b.fc.aliyuncs.com)
  region             Default region (e.g. cn-hangzhou, cn-shanghai)
  http_timeout       HTTP request timeout in seconds (number, e.g. 120)
  http2              Enable HTTP/2 (true/false)
  max_retries        Maximum retry attempts (integer, e.g. 3)
  llm_api_key        LLM API key for template generation,
                     e.g. a DashScope/ModelStudio key (string; stored in
                     ~/.abx/.env as ABX_LLM_API_KEY)
  llm_model          LLM model name (default: qwen3-coder-plus)
  llm_base_url       LLM API base URL, OpenAI-compatible (string;
                     default: DashScope compatible-mode)
  github_token       GitHub token for template downloads, used by
                     'abx template install' / 'abx template search'
                     (string; stored in ~/.abx/.env)

Examples:
  abx config set sandbox_api_key YOUR_API_KEY
  abx config set access_key_id YOUR_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  abx config set access_key_secret YOUR_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  abx config set acr_namespace YOUR_ACR_NAMESPACE
  abx config set region cn-hangzhou
  abx config set http_timeout 120
  abx config set http2 false
  abx config set llm_api_key YOUR_DASHSCOPE_OR_LLM_KEY
  abx config set region ""          # clear the stored region
  abx config set sandbox_api_key ""  # remove the stored sandbox API key
  abx config set github_token      # masked prompt (VALUE omitted)
  abx config set github_token YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN
  abx config set github_token ""    # remove the stored token

Related commands:
  abx config get KEY       Verify the effective value
  abx config list          Review effective values and sources
  abx config delete KEY    Remove one stored value

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

```

Usage: abx config list [options]

List all effective configuration values and their sources.

Values are grouped by function — Sandbox authentication, Alibaba
Cloud credentials, connection, LLM and integrations —
in a stable order. Group titles are
display-only: ``config get`` and ``config set`` keep taking the bare
key names, and ``--json`` output stays a flat ``{key: value}`` map.

Sources: ``(env)`` a process environment variable, ``(user)`` a value
in ``./.env`` or stored with ``abx config set``, ``(default)`` a
built-in default, and ``(not set)`` when no value exists anywhere.
A set environment variable wins over either file. ``./.env`` wins

``~/.abx``. Sensitive values are always masked.

### config-init --help

```
$ abx config init --help
Usage: abx config init [options]

Guided setup: credentials and region (add --build / --llm for the rest).

The default flow asks only what every command needs: the platform API
key and the default region. Press Enter to skip a prompt. Secrets are
typed with asterisk feedback (never echoed) when the terminal supports
it and stored in ~/.abx/.env; the region goes to ~/.abx/config.toml.

``--build`` adds the template build & push settings: the ACR namespace
and the Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pair (needed by ``abx template
install``, ``build``, ``push`` and ``deploy``).

``--llm`` adds the LLM API key used for template generation
(``abx create "<description>"``, ``abx template scaffold "<description>"``).

Features that need those settings print a pointer to ``abx config init
--build`` / ``--llm`` when they are missing; nothing asks for them up
front.

In non-TTY environments (CI, piped input) the wizard never blocks: it
prints the equivalent non-interactive ``abx config set ...`` commands
and exits successfully. ``--yes`` behaves the same way.

Examples:
  abx config init                 # credentials + region
  abx config init --build         # ... plus ACR namespace and AccessKey
  abx config init --llm           # ... plus the LLM API key
  abx config init --yes           # print non-interactive commands

Related commands:
  abx config list           Review effective values and sources
  abx config set KEY VALUE  Set one value directly
  abx config set KEY ""     Clear one stored value

Options:
  -y, --yes   Non-interactive: print the equivalent commands instead of
              prompting
  --build     Also ask for the selected provider build settings
  --llm       Also ask for the LLM API key used for template generation
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### template-build --help

```
$ abx template build --help
Usage: abx template build [options] [TEMPLATE_DIR]

Build Docker image locally, push to ACR, and create a sandbox template.

Full pipeline with cloud side effects: the local docker build is
local-only, but the ACR push and the remote template registration
can incur Alibaba Cloud costs (ACR storage/traffic, template
resources).

Publish path (--build, default auto):

auto: a Dockerfile publishes that image. Otherwise template.yaml build
  steps are sent as CreateTemplate sandboxConfig.steps.
dockerfile: local docker build → ACR push → CreateTemplate. template.yaml
  build steps are not sent.
steps: no local Docker and no ACR push. sandboxConfig.image is base.image
  and sandboxConfig.steps is the expanded build block. Official API only.

Registration API:

--official-api (default):
  dockerfile mode: local docker build → ACR push → official CreateTemplate API.
  Requires AK/SK credentials (set with 'abx config init --build').

--legacy-api:
  local docker build → ACR push → legacy v3/v2 platform API.
  Use --legacy-api to keep the old behaviour.

A missing directory offers interactive template creation and then continues.
--yes/-y or CI mode creates a Python template project without prompts.
Existing project files are kept.

Requires Docker daemon running and ACR credentials. In automation/CI,
pass --acr-namespace and TEMPLATE_DIR explicitly instead of relying
on ACR_NAMESPACE / ABX_TEMPLATE_DIR environment variables or .env
files, so the build cannot drift with the surrounding environment.

Examples:
  abx template build ./examples/templates/python-hello \
    --acr-namespace my-ns --acr-repo python-hello
  abx template build ./my-template \
    --acr-namespace prod --acree-instance-id cri-xxx
  abx template build ./my-template \
    --acr-namespace prod --disk-size 10240 --internet-access
  abx template build ./my-template \
    --acr-namespace prod --legacy-api
  abx template build ./my-template --acr-namespace prod --region cn-shanghai
  abx template build ./my-template --build steps --yes

Related commands:
  abx template scaffold DIRECTORY    Scaffold template source files
  abx template push IMAGE        Push an existing local image only
  abx create ID       Launch the completed template

Options:
  --acr-registry <ACR_REGISTRY>            ACR registry host
  --acr-namespace <ACR_NAMESPACE>          ACR namespace (env: ACR_NAMESPACE, or set in .env file)
  --acr-repo <ACR_REPO>                    ACR repository name (defaults to template.yaml name or dir name)
  --acr-username <ACR_USERNAME>            ACR login username (default: ALICLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID)
  --acr-password <ACR_PASSWORD>            ACR login password (default: ALICLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET)
  --acree-instance-id <ACREE_INSTANCE_ID>  ACR EE instance ID (cri-...)
  --vpc-id <VPC_ID>                        VPC ID for ACR EE
  --vswitch-ids <VSWITCH_IDS>              Comma-separated VSwitch IDs
  --security-group-id <SECURITY_GROUP_ID>  Security group ID
  -a, --alias <ALIAS>                      Template alias
  -t, --tag <TAG>                          Docker image tag
  --platform <PLATFORM>                    Target platform
  --cpu <INTEGER>                          CPU cores (default: from template.yaml resources.cpu, fallback 2)
  --memory <INTEGER>                       Memory in MB (default: from template.yaml resources.memory, fallback 2048)
  --start-cmd <START_CMD>                  Container start command
  --ready-cmd <READY_CMD>                  Container readiness check command
  --timeout <INTEGER>                      Build timeout in seconds
  -f, --dockerfile <PATH>                  Custom Dockerfile path
  --build <BUILD>                          Publish path: auto (Dockerfile if present, otherwise template.yaml build steps), dockerfile, or steps [default: auto] (choices: "auto", "dockerfile", "steps")
  --disk-size <INTEGER>                    Disk size in MB (official API only)
  --internet-access                        Internet access (default: platform decides; official API only)
  --no-internet-access                     Opposite of --internet-access.
  --official-api                           Use official CreateTemplate API (default) or legacy v3/v2
  --legacy-api                             Opposite of --official-api.
  --team-id <TEAM_ID>                      Team ID for official API (or env TEAM_ID / E2B_TEAM_ID)
  --envd-inject                            Enable envd injection (default False)
  --no-envd-inject                         Opposite of --envd-inject.
  --generation <INTEGER>                   Sandbox generation (default: template.yaml 'generation'; else 2 when the provider starts the server and commands.py exists; else 1). 1=first-gen (rund), 2=second-gen MicroVM.
  --force                                  If a generation-1 template with this name already exists, delete it and create it again. Without --force, deploy stops and prints 'abx template delete <id> -y'.
  --target-image <TARGET_IMAGE>            Destination image ref for envd copy (auto-derived with random suffix if omitted)
  -y, --yes                                Skip confirmation prompt
  -v, --verbose                            Verbose output (DEBUG level)
  -r, --region <TEXT>                      Region override for providers that declare region (otherwise use the provider default)
  -h, --help                               Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### template-init --help

```
$ abx template scaffold --help
Usage: abx template scaffold [options] [DIRECTORY]

Scaffold a new sandbox template project.

Creates a ready-to-build template directory with template.yaml,
Dockerfile, and (depending on the case) a commands.py file.
Nothing is built, pushed, deployed, or turned into a sandbox.

When DIRECTORY is omitted a new ./<name> subdirectory is created
(derived from --name, the scaffold case, or the fetched template).
Existing nonempty directories show the affected entries before writing.
Interactive replacement requires confirmation; in scripts use --force
explicitly. --yes alone never authorizes overwriting existing entries.

--prompt requests natural-language template generation; DIRECTORY always
names a directory. Template generation (Qwen Code, needs 'abx config init
--llm')
writes Dockerfile, commands.py (the HTTP server) and template.yaml into
./<name>/ and stops. An interactive
terminal is asked for that directory first (Enter keeps ./<name>/).
A path token (my-app, ./my app) stays a directory.

--adopt adapts a project that already has source code and no template
files. Template generation sees a copy, and only Dockerfile, commands.py,
template.yaml and a generated .dockerignore are written back, after you
confirm. Nothing is built or deployed.

Examples:
  abx template scaffold --list                     # List built-in cases
  abx template scaffold -t python                  # Creates ./python/
  abx template scaffold -t python --name myapp     # Creates ./myapp/
  abx template scaffold -t python ./my-template    # Explicit directory
  abx template scaffold --from owner/repo          # Creates ./<template-name>/
  abx template scaffold --prompt "a python data science env"  # generate files
only, no build
  abx template scaffold -y --prompt "a node.js api server"    # non-interactive
generation
  abx template scaffold --adopt . --hint "port 8080" # adapt this project
  abx template scaffold --adopt ./app --dry-run      # show what would be sent

Related commands:
  abx template deploy DIRECTORY
  abx template install TEMPLATE_REF
  abx create TEMPLATE
  abx create --prompt "DESCRIPTION"   # generate, build, deploy, and create

Options:
  --prompt <PROMPT>      Generate a template from a natural-language description
  -t, --template <CASE>  Built-in scaffold case (python, node, minimal)
  --from <FROM_REF>      Fetch template source from a registry ref (owner/repo,
                         local path)
  --name <NAME>          Template name (default: case name, or fetched template
                         name)
  --list                 List available scaffold cases
  --force                Overwrite existing files
  --adopt                Adapt an existing source project: template generation
                         adds the template files (Dockerfile, commands.py,
                         template.yaml). DIRECTORY is the project (default: .).
  --hint <HINT>          With --adopt: what the code cannot tell the generator
                         (ports, services).
  --dry-run              With --adopt: list what would be sent to the model.
                         Nothing is sent or written.
  -v, --verbose          Verbose output (DEBUG level)
  -y, --yes              Skip confirmation prompts: the template directory,
                         description clarification, and (with --adopt) the send
                         and write prompts. Required for non-interactive
                         template generation. Does not build or deploy.
                         Replacing an existing Dockerfile still needs --force
                         when there is no interactive preview.
  --model <MODEL>        Model id for natural-language generation. Overrides
                         llm_model for this command. An interactive terminal
                         offers coding and chat models with the arrow keys when
                         the chosen id does not exist.
  -h, --help             Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### template-install --help

```
$ abx template install --help
Usage: abx template install [options] <TEMPLATE_REF>

Download a template and (by default) build + deploy it.

By default, install downloads the template, then runs docker build,
pushes to ACR, and creates a sandbox template via the official API —
cloud-side operations that can incur Alibaba Cloud costs (ACR
storage/traffic, template resources). Use --download-only to skip the
build/deploy step and only download to the local cache
(~/.abx/templates/).

Use --dir <path> to download into a specific directory instead of
the cache.

TEMPLATE_REF can be a bare template name from the official index
(alibaba-agent-sandbox/awesome-templates) or a registry reference. Bare names
are resolved against the remote index; entries may pin a version, in
which case that pinned ref is honoured.

A GitHub token (private repos / higher rate limits) is taken from
--token, then the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, then ./.env, then
the stored github_token; prefer 'abx config set github_token' - --token
may leak into shell history and process listings.

Examples:
  abx template install python-hello --download-only   # install by index name
  abx template install owner/repo --acr-namespace my-ns
  abx template install owner/repo@v1.0 --download-only
  abx template install owner/repo//subdir --dir ./local-copy
  abx template install owner/repo --acr-namespace my-ns --region cn-shanghai

Related commands:
  abx template search QUERY  Find a template in the index
  abx template list          List registered templates
  abx create ID   Launch the installed template

Options:
  --registry-url <REGISTRY_URL>    Registry URL (default: GitHub)
  --registry-type <REGISTRY_TYPE>  Registry type (auto-detected if not
                                   specified) (choices: "github", "local")
  --token <TOKEN>                  GitHub token for private repos / higher rate
                                   limits. Prefer 'abx config set github_token'
                                   (masked input, stored once in ~/.abx/.env);
                                   --token is a temporary override that may leak
                                   into shell history and the process list (env:
                                   GITHUB_TOKEN).
  -a, --alias <ALIAS>              Template alias
  --download-only                  Only download to local cache (skip build and
                                   deploy)
  --dir <PATH>                     Download template source into this directory
                                   instead of the cache
  --acr-namespace <ACR_NAMESPACE>  ACR namespace for deploy (env: ACR_NAMESPACE,
                                   or set in .env file)
  --cpu <INTEGER>                  CPU cores (default: from template.yaml or 2)
  --memory <INTEGER>               Memory in MB (default: from template.yaml or
                                   2048)
  -y, --yes                        Skip confirmation prompt
  -r, --region <TEXT>              Region override for providers that declare
                                   region (otherwise use the provider default)
  -h, --help                       Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### mcp --help

```
$ abx mcp --help
Usage: abx mcp [options] [command]

Configure and run Agent Sandbox as an MCP server.

Use local STDIO transport for IDE integrations, or generate a Streamable
HTTP deployment artifact for manual deployment to Alibaba Cloud FC.

Examples:
  abx mcp install --target cursor
  abx mcp start
  abx mcp start --http --background
  abx mcp stop
  abx mcp deploy --generate-token --output-dir ./mcp-artifact

Related commands:
  abx config set sandbox_api_key VALUE  Configure sandbox authentication
  abx mcp status                Inspect local MCP configuration
  abx mcp stop                  Stop the local MCP server

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  deploy      Generate an Alibaba Cloud FC deployment artifact.
  install     Install MCP Server configuration to a target IDE.
  start       Start the MCP server and print its configuration to stderr.
  status      Show MCP tools, authentication state, and IDE installation status.
  stop        Stop the local MCP server started by 'abx mcp start'.
Exit code: 0
```

### mcp-deploy --help

```
$ abx mcp deploy --help
Usage: abx mcp deploy [options]

Generate an Alibaba Cloud FC deployment artifact.

Creates a Streamable HTTP ASGI application artifact and prints manual
FC deployment steps. Automatic FC API deployment is not implemented.

The artifact contains ``requirements.txt``, ``app.py`` (ASGI entry
point), and ``config.yaml`` (a YAML deployment manifest with FC function
settings and environment variables).

``--region`` overrides the FC region for this invocation; without it the
region comes from ``abx config set region`` / ``ALIBABA_CLOUD_REGION_ID``
environment variable and defaults to ``cn-hangzhou``.

A non-empty Bearer token is required (--generate-token or
--auth-token-file). POST and DELETE /mcp are implemented. GET /mcp
returns 405 until SSE server notifications exist. The function
environment sets ALIBABA_CLOUD_REGION_ID to the selected region.

Examples:
  abx mcp deploy --generate-token --api-key $ABX_SANDBOX_API_KEY
  abx mcp deploy --auth-token-file ./token.txt --region cn-shanghai
  abx mcp deploy --generate-token --output-dir ./deploy-artifact

Related commands:
  abx mcp start                 Run the local STDIO server
  abx mcp status                Inspect MCP authentication state
  abx config set sandbox_api_key VALUE  Configure sandbox authentication

Options:
  --name <NAME>                    FC function name for the artifact.
  -r, --region <TEXT>              Region override for providers that declare
                                   region (otherwise use the provider default)
  --template <TEMPLATE>            Default sandbox template for MCP sessions.
  --memory <INTEGER>               FC function memory (MB).
  --timeout <INTEGER>              FC function timeout (s).
  --auth-token-file <PATH>         Path to a non-empty Bearer token file.
  --generate-token                 Auto-generate a random Bearer token.
  --enable-session-affinity        Enable Mcp-Session-Id affinity (requires FC
                                   MCP support).
  --no-session-affinity            Opposite of --enable-session-affinity.
  --api-key <API_KEY>              ABX_SANDBOX_API_KEY to inject into the FC
                                   function env.
  --custom-domain <CUSTOM_DOMAIN>  Custom domain for the MCP endpoint.
  --output-dir <PATH>              Write the FC deployment artifact to this
                                   directory.
  -h, --help                       Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### mcp-start --help

```
$ abx mcp start --help
Usage: abx mcp start [options]

Start the MCP server and print its configuration to stderr.

The default transport is STDIO: an IDE writes JSON-RPC to stdin and reads
responses from stdout. Run it in a terminal to see the configuration and
stop it with Ctrl-C or 'abx mcp stop'.

--http listens for Streamable HTTP. --background detaches that HTTP
server; STDIO cannot keep a client attached after detach, so --background
starts HTTP.

Examples:
  abx mcp start
  abx mcp start --template python-hello
  abx mcp start --http --port 9000
  abx mcp start --http --background
  abx mcp stop

Related commands:
  abx mcp install --target cursor  Register the STDIO command in an IDE
  abx mcp stop                     Stop the local MCP server
  abx mcp status                   Check authentication and IDE setup

Options:
  --template <TEMPLATE>      Default sandbox template ID or alias (default:
                             code-interpreter-v1).
  --api-key <API_KEY>        API key override.
  --api-url <API_URL>        API URL override.
  --domain <DOMAIN>          Domain override.
  --http                     Serve Streamable HTTP instead of STDIO.
  --host <HOST>              HTTP bind address. [default: 127.0.0.1]
  --port <INTEGER>           HTTP bind port. [default: 9000]
  --auth-token <AUTH_TOKEN>  Bearer token for the HTTP server. Required when
                             --host is not loopback.
  --background               Detach an HTTP server. Stop it later with 'abx mcp
                             stop'.
  -h, --help                 Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### mcp-stop --help

```
$ abx mcp stop --help
Usage: abx mcp stop [options]

Stop the local MCP server started by 'abx mcp start'.

Sends SIGTERM to the recorded pid (STDIO foreground or HTTP background)
and waits for it to exit. Sandboxes owned by that server are destroyed
during its shutdown.

Examples:
  abx mcp stop

Related commands:
  abx mcp start            Start STDIO in the foreground
  abx mcp start --http --background
  abx mcp status           Inspect configuration and whether a server is running

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```

### deploy --help

```
$ abx deploy --help
Usage: abx deploy [options] [PATH]

Publish a template project: build, push to ACR, register the template (same as
'abx template deploy').

Runs one publish path. No LLM is involved.
PATH is the template directory (default: .). --build auto (the default)
uses a Dockerfile when one is present, and otherwise template.yaml build
steps. dockerfile mode builds and pushes an image, then waits until the
template is ready. steps mode sends base.image and sandboxConfig.steps
and does not use Docker or ACR. template.yaml supplies the template name
and resources.

A missing PATH offers template creation and continues after confirmation.
--yes/-y or CI mode creates a Python template project without prompts.
Existing project files are kept.

To author the files first, use 'abx template scaffold': --adopt for an existing
project, a natural-language description to generate the files, or
--template for a scaffold.

Accepts every option of 'abx template deploy' (--acr-namespace,
--alias, --yes, -v/--verbose, ...). The ACR namespace and AccessKey are
set with 'abx config init --build'.

Examples:
  abx deploy --acr-namespace my-ns           # publish ./ as a template
  abx deploy ./my-template --yes             # non-interactive
  abx --json deploy ./my-template -y         # JSON on stdout; id is TemplateID
  abx deploy ./my-template -v                # with debug logs

Typical flow:
  abx template scaffold --adopt .                      # 1a. author from a
project
  abx template scaffold --prompt "a python data science env"   # 1b. generate
from a description
  abx deploy ./<name> --acr-namespace my-ns       # 2. publish
  abx create <TEMPLATE_ID>             # 3. launch a sandbox

Related commands:
  abx template scaffold          Author Dockerfile / template.yaml
  abx template deploy DIR    The same pipeline with a required DIRECTORY
  abx create "DESCRIPTION"   Generate + publish + launch in one go

Options:
  --acr-registry <ACR_REGISTRY>            ACR registry host
  --acr-namespace <ACR_NAMESPACE>          ACR namespace (env: ACR_NAMESPACE, or set in .env file)
  --acr-repo <ACR_REPO>                    ACR repository name (defaults to template.yaml name or dir name)
  --acr-username <ACR_USERNAME>            ACR login username (default: ALICLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID)
  --acr-password <ACR_PASSWORD>            ACR login password (default: ALICLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET)
  --acree-instance-id <ACREE_INSTANCE_ID>  ACR EE instance ID (cri-...)
  --vpc-id <VPC_ID>                        VPC ID for ACR EE
  --vswitch-ids <VSWITCH_IDS>              Comma-separated VSwitch IDs
  --security-group-id <SECURITY_GROUP_ID>  Security group ID
  -a, --alias <ALIAS>                      Template alias
  -t, --tag <TAG>                          Docker image tag
  --platform <PLATFORM>                    Target platform
  --cpu <INTEGER>                          CPU cores (default: from template.yaml resources.cpu, fallback 2)
  --memory <INTEGER>                       Memory in MB (default: from template.yaml resources.memory, fallback 2048)
  --start-cmd <START_CMD>                  Container start command
  --ready-cmd <READY_CMD>                  Container readiness check command
  --timeout <INTEGER>                      Build timeout in seconds
  -f, --dockerfile <PATH>                  Custom Dockerfile path
  --build <BUILD>                          Publish path: auto (Dockerfile if present, otherwise template.yaml build steps), dockerfile, or steps [default: auto] (choices: "auto", "dockerfile", "steps")
  --disk-size <INTEGER>                    Disk size in MB (official API only)
  --internet-access                        Internet access (default: platform decides; official API only)
  --no-internet-access                     Opposite of --internet-access.
  --official-api                           Use official CreateTemplate API (default) or legacy v3/v2
  --legacy-api                             Opposite of --official-api.
  --team-id <TEAM_ID>                      Team ID for official API (or env TEAM_ID / E2B_TEAM_ID)
  --envd-inject                            Enable envd injection (default False)
  --no-envd-inject                         Opposite of --envd-inject.
  --generation <INTEGER>                   Sandbox generation (default: template.yaml 'generation'; else 2 when the provider starts the server and commands.py exists; else 1). 1=first-gen (rund), 2=second-gen MicroVM.
  --force                                  If a generation-1 template with this name already exists, delete it and create it again. Without --force, deploy stops and prints 'abx template delete <id> -y'.
  --target-image <TARGET_IMAGE>            Destination image ref for envd copy (auto-derived with random suffix if omitted)
  -y, --yes                                Skip confirmation prompt
  -v, --verbose                            Verbose output (DEBUG level)
  -r, --region <TEXT>                      Region override for providers that declare region (otherwise use the provider default)
  -h, --help                               Show this message and exit.
Exit code: 0
```
